action: Store passwords only hashed with a current algorithm, give each employee an individual account for customer databases, and purge contact-form and connection data on a schedule.
date_note: CNIL published the sanction on 18 November 2026; its page links deliberation SAN-2026-016 of 12 November 2026.
exec: France's CNIL fined an unnamed company 5 million euros for security failings, including plaintext password storage; weak password handling can now carry a large GDPR penalty.
plain: France's data protection regulator fined a company it chose not to name 5 million euros, partly because customer passwords were stored in plain text.

key_findings: Customer account passwords were stored in plaintext (conservés en clair), breaching GDPR article 32.
Credentials for customer databases and the access tool were shared among several employees.
Contact-form data was kept for more than 10 years; connection data beyond the company's own one-year policy.
recommendations: Delete data once the request is handled.

summary: CNIL, the French data protection authority, announced on 18 November a fine of 5 million euros on a company it chose not to name. It says customer account passwords were stored in plaintext, breaching GDPR article 32. CNIL also cites shared employee credentials for customer databases and contact-form data kept for more than 10 years. It mentions no data breach.
title: CNIL fines unnamed company 5 million euros over plaintext password storage

validation.note: CNIL's own page read in full; Security.nl relays it. Security.nl adds figures (1.8 million customers, hashing detail) that the CNIL page does not state, so they are not used.
